aod.name: Aerosol haze (optical depth)
aod.plain: How much sunlight is blocked by tiny particles in the air, such as smoke, dust and pollution. 0 is perfectly clear; above 0.5 is very hazy.
aod.why: Cleaner factories and cars can make the air clearer, while growing cities, fires and dust storms can make it hazier.

u250.name: East-west wind at 250 hPa
u250.plain: How fast the wind blows toward the east (positive) or west (negative) about 10 km up, at jet-stream height.
u250.why: The jet stream is driven by the temperature difference between the poles and the tropics, so it can strengthen, weaken or shift as that difference changes.

v250.name: North-south wind at 250 hPa
v250.plain: How fast the wind blows toward the north (positive) or south (negative) about 10 km up.
v250.why: A wavier jet stream has stronger north-south winds, which can bring longer spells of hot or cold weather.

velocity.name: Climate velocity
velocity.plain: How fast, in kilometres per decade, a place would have to move to keep the same value: the trend divided by how quickly the value changes across the map.
velocity.why: A small trend in a flat region (an ocean, a plain) moves the value a long way; the same trend on a steep mountainside barely moves it.

fzlev.name: Freezing level height
fzlev.plain: How high above sea level you have to climb before the air is colder than 0 °C. Glaciers and snow can only last above it.
fzlev.why: When the air warms, the 0 °C level rises up mountainsides, so snow turns to rain and glaciers melt higher up.
